prompt: In parallelogram $ABCD$, $\angle A = 68^\circ$. What is the measure of $\angle B$, the angle next to it, in degrees?
hint: In a parallelogram, angles that sit next to each other are supplementary — they add to $180^\circ$.

hints.text: In a parallelogram, angles that sit next to each other are supplementary — they add to $180^\circ$.

explanation: Opposite sides of a parallelogram are parallel, so consecutive angles are same-side interior angles and add to $180^\circ$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Check all four
steps: Opposite angles are equal, so the four angles are $68^\circ$, $112^\circ$, $68^\circ$, $112^\circ$.
They total $68 + 112 + 68 + 112 = 360^\circ$ ✓ — exactly what a quadrilateral should have.
